sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: Modal verbs express ability, obligation, permission and intention — and they push the main verb to the end.

blocks.text: A modal verb takes the second position in the sentence and the main verb moves to the end as an infinitive: Ich muss heute länger arbeiten. The modal is conjugated, the infinitive never changes.

The six core modals are können (can), müssen (must), dürfen (may), wollen (want), sollen (should) and mögen (like). Their ich and er/sie/es forms are identical and often have no ending: ich kann, er kann; ich muss, sie muss.

blocks.title: The sentence bracket
blocks.text: Think of the modal and the infinitive as two halves of a bracket: Ich [muss] heute länger [arbeiten]. Everything else sits inside it.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

rows: Wir wollen ins Kino. Du sollst warten. Ich mag Kaffee.

items: The main verb is an infinitive at the very end of the clause.
Modal verbs have no ending in the ich and er/sie/es forms.
Use könnte and würde for polite requests: Könnten Sie mir helfen?

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Notice how the pattern behaves in a complete sentence.

items.en: I have to work longer today.
items.note: The infinitive arbeiten closes the sentence.
The modal starts a yes/no question.

items.en: You are not allowed to smoke here.
items.note: The infinitive rauchen goes to the end.
Könnten is the polite form of können.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

items.hint: The ü is rounded: say “ee” with rounded lips, then a short -ssen.
The ü is long and rounded; the final -en is soft.
The ö is rounded like the vowel in “bird”, but shorter.

blocks.text: German public life runs on clear rules, and signs often state what is forbidden rather than what is allowed: “Rauchen verboten”, “Betreten verboten”. Understanding dürfen and müssen helps you read them quickly.
At work, sollen often expresses an instruction from a manager rather than a moral duty. A polite “Soll ich das bis Freitag erledigen?” is a normal way to confirm a task.

sections.title: Dialogue in context
sections.lede: Read the scene, then play it and follow the speakers.
sections.setting: At the office, Lea asks her manager about tomorrow’s schedule.

lines.speaker: Chef
lines.de: Ja, aber du musst bis zehn Uhr im Büro sein.
lines.en: Yes, but you have to be in the office by ten.

lines.speaker: Lea
lines.de: Danke. Darf ich dann von zu Hause arbeiten?
lines.en: Thanks. May I work from home then?

lines.speaker: Chef
lines.de: Das können wir machen. Schick mir bitte eine E-Mail.
lines.en: We can do that. Please send me an email.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Modal verbs and the sentence bracket
sections.lede: The modal is conjugated in position two; the main verb stays in the infinitive at the end.

blocks.text: Möchte is the polite form of wollen and is extremely common in shops and restaurants: Ich möchte einen Kaffee, bitte.

sections.tip: Learn each modal with its ich form first. The ich and er/sie/es forms are the same, which removes half the endings you expected.

sections.title: Listening
sections.lede: Listen twice before you look at the transcript.
sections.speaker: Am Telefon

script.speaker: Kunde
script.de: Guten Tag, kann ich meinen Termin verschieben?
script.en: Hello, can I move my appointment?

script.speaker: Praxis
script.de: Ja, das können wir machen. Wann möchten Sie kommen?
script.en: Yes, we can do that. When would you like to come?

script.speaker: Kunde
script.de: Am Donnerstag. Ich muss aber bis vier Uhr arbeiten.
script.en: On Thursday. But I have to work until four.

script.speaker: Praxis
script.de: Dann geben wir Ihnen einen Termin um halb fünf.
script.en: Then we will give you an appointment at half past four.

questions.prompt: What does the customer want to do?
questions.explanation: The customer asks “Kann ich meinen Termin verschieben?”, to move the appointment.

questions.prompt: Why can’t the customer come before four?
questions.explanation: He says “Ich muss aber bis vier Uhr arbeiten.”

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Say two things you must do this week and one thing you are allowed to do. Use modal verbs.

model.de: Ich muss am Montag arbeiten. Ich muss auch meine Eltern anrufen. Am Freitag darf ich früher nach Hause gehen.
model.en: I have to work on Monday. I also have to call my parents. On Friday I may go home earlier.

tips: Keep the modal in second position and the infinitive at the end.
Use darf for permission and muss for obligation.
Add a time phrase such as am Montag directly after the modal.
